title: Natural Pools or a Boat Swim: Where Is Madeira's Best Sea Swim?
description: Natural pools at Porto Moniz, Seixal and Funchal give calm, guarded water. A swim stop from a boat gives deep open sea under cliffs with nobody else around.
heroAlt: Calm natural lava pools at Seixal on Madeira's north coast, waves breaking beyond the rocks
keywords: natural pools or swimming from a boat Madeira

images.prompt: Early morning at the natural lava pools of Seixal on Madeira's north coast: calm green-blue sea water held in basins of black volcanic rock in the foreground, white Atlantic waves breaking on the outer rocks beyond, and steep green mountainsides with a few white houses rising behind under soft light. Two swimmers seen small and from behind float in the far pool. No boat, natural light, true colours, no text, no logos.
images.alt: Calm natural lava pools at Seixal on Madeira's north coast, waves breaking beyond the rocks

images.prompt: From water level, a swimmer seen from behind floats in deep dark blue sea a few metres from the stern of a white 9 metre motor boat with grey cushioned seats and a dark canopy, the tall brown and green cliff of Madeira's south coast above, late morning.
images.alt: A swimmer in deep open water beside a private boat under Madeira's cliffs

images.prompt: Drone view from above the natural swimming pools of Porto Moniz in Madeira: geometric basins of turquoise water set in black lava rock, waves breaking white along the outer wall, the small islet with its lighthouse offshore, midday, people tiny.
images.alt: The lava rock swimming pools of Porto Moniz seen from above
